newsitem.title: MEXICO: Brazil sugar expansions depend on price - ISO.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sugar expansions depend on price - ISO.

text.p: Unless prices fall from current ranges, Brazil may be expected to continue expanding sugar production, the head of the economics and statistics division of the International Sugar Organisation (ISO) said Wednesday.
Tony Hannah told the F.O. Licht World Sugar and Sweetners' Conference here that any further expansion would be at a slower rate than in the first half of the 1990s though.
Production grew to 13.8 million tonnes in 1995 from eight million tonnes in 1990, an increase of 5.8 million tonnes or 72 percent.
Hannah said a number of factors combined to build the massive expansion. One, he said, was that alcohol demand stabilised as the number of purely alcohol driven cars began to decline.

Also, increased cane availability due to good weather and increased yields went into sugar production. "Exports were profitable. For a time, importing alcohol and exporting sugar was profitable," he said.
